# Spore drive

The **spore drive**, formally known as the **displacement-activated spore hub drive**, is a fictional spacecraft propulsion system introduced in the 2017 television series Star Trek: Discovery . It is an organic propulsion system that utilizes mycelium spores from the fungus Prototaxites stellaviatori to facilitate near-instantaneous travel across vast distances through an intergalactic mycelial network .

## Origins and development

The spore drive was developed by two colleagues and friends, Paul Stamets and Justin Straal, who had been working on the concept since 2244 . Both Stamets and Straal were astromycologists who collaborated on the technology . Their research was based on the insight that at a quantum level, there was no difference between biology and physics, and specifically that spores were not only the progenitors of panspermia, but also the building blocks of energy across the universe .

The technology was jointly deployed on two vessels: the USS Glenn and the USS Discovery . These ships were part of the Crossfield-class, a starship class specifically designed around the experimental drive . After war broke out between the Federation and the Klingon Empire in May 2256, the Discovery and her sister ship, the USS Glenn, were tasked by Starfleet with a top-secret mission to develop this new kind of faster-than-light drive .

The Glenn managed to perfect the drive through the acquisition of a creature referred to as a tardigrade, which served as a navigator through the mycelial network . However, the Glenn's crew, along with Straal, were all killed in an accident that ensued during a failed jump . Following this disaster, the Discovery acquired the tardigrade from the Glenn and its crew managed to successfully use the technology in the following months .

## Technical specifications

The spore drive represents a fundamental departure from conventional Star Trek propulsion technologies such as impulse drive and warp drive . Instead of traveling slower-than-light (via impulse engines) or faster-than-light through space (via warp drive), the spore drive enables an instantaneous "jump" from one location in space to another, disconnected place a great distance away .

The drive operates by utilizing mycelium spores harvested from Prototaxites stellaviatori to "jump" or "leap" across the mycelial network . During such jumps, the ships are not in normal space but in the mycelial plane . A ship utilizing spore drive exists inside the mycelial network for only a few milliseconds during a jump .

The technology has no theoretical speed limit. From an outside perspective, the ship disappears and reappears in another location almost instantly . The USS Glenn completed a jump of 90 light-years in 1.3 seconds, though they encountered a Hawking radiation firewall during this attempt .

Distance displacement is measured in a unit called **Speirein**, with higher Speireins being associated with larger displacement . Jumping is probabilistic, meaning that the longer the jump, the more possible outcomes there are. The technology requires extensive computational power to calculate jump trajectories, and current computers lack the processing capacity to make the requisite number of calculations for long jumps, resulting in navigational instability . Some six months after the start of the war, the Discovery had reached Speirein 12, enabling jumps measured in the hundreds of kilometers .

The spore drive's operation involves several key components and processes:

1. **Reaction cube**: The chamber in which spores are injected, with one possible density being 68%

2. **Spore germination rate**: A critical factor in drive operation

3. **Excess energy cavitation**: Part of the initiation process 

4. **Specific deactivation sequence**: Required to prevent the induction coil from becoming saturated 

All personnel working around the spore drive are inoculated as a safety precaution . A level 3 diagnostic is run on the entire spore drive every ten hours .

## Navigation and limitations

The spore drive's navigation system initially relied on the tardigrade's natural connection to the mycelial network. When the tardigrade began dying, Stamets conducted an illegal genetic augmentation on himself using tardigrade DNA to take over the navigator role personally .

The drive's stamina is not limited by the technology itself but by the endurance of the "pilot" navigating the mycelial network . Each jump requires the pilot to "feel" their way through the network. While a few jumps in succession are not difficult, the USS Discovery's record of 133 jumps in rapid succession severely strained Stamets .

Potential risks associated with the spore drive include:

* **Unintended interdimensional travel**: The drive can potentially access alternate universes, as demonstrated by the Discovery's jump to the Mirror Universe

* **Time travel**: The mycelial network exists outside normal space-time, creating temporal paradox risks

* **Network pollution**: Improper use can contaminate the mycelial network

* **Partial jumps**: A partial jump on a predetermined course with no set end point could leave the ship half in, half out of the network, essentially functioning as a "doorstop" 

## Program history

Following the conclusion of the Federation-Klingon War in 2257, Starfleet decommissioned the drive until a non-human interface could be developed . The technology was classified with the disappearance of the Discovery .

In 2258, Captain Christopher Pike authorized the use of the drive to travel 51,450 light years to the planet Terralysium to investigate one of the red bursts, believing the crisis worthy of special dispensation .

In 3189, during the refitting of the Discovery, a new and improved spore drive interface was installed . Instead of mechanically connecting to the pilot via cybernetic shunts, the pilot merely had to rest their hands on nanogel control pads, with the gel acting as a quantum transducer . The ship's nacelles had to be attached before the drive could be activated .

A second-generation spore drive was developed with a prototype able to be quickly and easily installed into any ship . It still required a compatible pilot .

## Reception and cultural impact

The introduction of the spore drive generated significant debate among Star Trek fans and critics . Some viewers considered it a bold new direction for the series, while others felt it strayed too far from established Star Trek lore .

Critics of the technology pointed to several issues:

1. **Lack of prior mention**: The spore drive had never been referenced in any previous Star Trek series or films, despite being a potentially game-changing technology that could essentially teleport ships across the galaxy .

2. **Departure from established physics**: The concept of using spores to achieve instantaneous travel seemed too far removed from the more grounded scientific principles that had traditionally underpinned Star Trek's warp drive technology .

3. **Impact on narrative tension**: Some viewers felt that the drive's near-instantaneous travel capabilities undermined the traditional Star Trek concept of exploration and the challenges of deep space travel .

However, supporters of the technology appreciated:

1. **Scientific innovation**: The drive represented an imaginative expansion of Star Trek's scientific universe, incorporating concepts from mycology and quantum biology .

2. **Character development opportunities**: The drive's development and operation provided rich narrative material for character arcs, particularly for Paul Stamets .

3. **Plot possibilities**: The drive enabled new storytelling opportunities, including interdimensional travel and time travel narratives .

The technology has been described as "far from the most ridiculous piece of science that Trek has done, but it gets a lot more flak because, rather than being something odd that happened in one episode, it became a recurring and integral part of the show" .

## Later developments

In the 33rd century, the crew used the spore drive one last time to send Discovery—returned to its pre-refit configuration—into deep space on a Red Directive mission where the ship would wait for nearly a thousand years for Craft .

In the 25th century, the Elachi make limited, but technically advanced use of spore drives on some of their ships due to their origin in the Mycelial network .

Considering the inherent risks of the spore drive—unintended interdimensional travel, time travel, and the risk to the navigator—the experimental drive has fallen out of favor with Starfleet . No current vessels in the Federation make use of it . With the continuing advancement of bio-neural technology, this may eventually change, but for the time being, Starfleet's engineering divisions remain focused on the development of Quantum Slipstream Drives .

## Legacy

The spore drive represents a significant innovation in Star Trek's fictional technology, introducing concepts of organic propulsion and quantum mycology that expanded the franchise's scientific universe . While controversial among fans, it 无疑推动了 Star Trek's narrative in new directions and provided memorable storylines involving interdimensional travel, time travel, and the ethical implications of advanced technology.

The technology's development also highlighted important themes about the relationship between science and ethics, as seen in Stamets' decision to undergo genetic augmentation to operate the drive . The spore drive's ultimate decommissioning due to its inherent risks serves as a cautionary tale about the potential dangers of technology that advances faster than our ability to understand and control it .

Despite its controversial reception, the spore drive remains a significant part of Star Trek: Discovery's legacy and a notable innovation in the franchise's technological mythology.

Spore drive
-----------

"_Imagine a microscopic web that spans the entire cosmos. An intergalactic ecosystem. An infinite number of roads leading everywhere._"— Gabriel Lorca
The **displacement-activated spore hub drive**, commonly shortened to **spore drive** (a slang term referring to a displacement-activated spore hub drive) or **s-drive**, was an organic propulsion system the [Federation](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Federation "Federation") experimented with during the 2240s and 2250s. The technology used mycelium spores harvested from _prototaxites stellaviatori_ to **jump** or **leap** across the mycelial network. During such jumps, the ships were not in normal space but in the mycelial plane.

*   [1 Origins and concept](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive#Origins_and_concept)
*   [2 Program history](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive#Program_history)
    *   [2.1 Current usage](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive#Current_usage)
    *   [2.2 Super-mycelial reactor](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive#Super-mycelial_reactor)

*   [3 Technical details](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive#Technical_details)

Origins and concept[[](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive?veaction=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Origins and concept")]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The spore drive was based on the ideas of two colleagues and friends, Paul Stamets and Straal, who had been working on the concept since 2244. They were eager to get to the "veins and muscles" that held the galaxy together.

Their research was based on the insight that at a quantum level, there was no difference between biology or physics, and specifically that spores were not only the progenitors of panspermia, but also the building blocks of energy across the universe. This allowed Stamets and Straal to approach physics as biology. As such, the equations involved were reminiscent of both quantum astrophysics and biochemistry.

Program history[[](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive?veaction=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Program history")]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Initially confined to a lab, following the outbreak of [war with the Klingons](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Federation-Klingon_War_(2256-57) "Federation-Klingon War (2256-57)"), [Starfleet](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Starfleet "Starfleet") co-opted the research for military applications, much to the displeasure of Stamets. The two scientists were split up and given two different teams on different vessels – the [USS _Discovery_](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Discovery_(NCC-1031) "USS Discovery (NCC-1031)") and the [USS _Glenn_](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Glenn_(NCC-1030) "USS Glenn (NCC-1030)") – so they could work twice as fast. The _Discovery_ also contained a large cultivation bay.

By late 2256, six months after the start of the war, both ships were conducting "black alert" maneuvers, in which they made jumps across the mycelial network. These jumps were associated with the ship's walls becoming damp. Containment of the spores was important to prevent accidents.

Key to the research was to increase the interval, which was expressed in Speirin, higher Speirins being associated with large displacement. Jumping was probabilistic, meaning that the longer the jump, the more possible outcomes there were. The two ships lacked the processing power to make the requisite number of calculations, and so long jumps resulted in navigational instability. Some six months after the start of the war, the _Discovery_ had reached Speirin 12 and leaps measured in the hundreds of kilometers. This was considered a poor result by _Discovery_ captain Gabriel Lorca. However, its sister ship _Glenn_ made a breakthrough and achieved Speirin 240. The fact that they did not grow their own spores somehow resulted in the acquisition of "Ripper", an Tardigrade resembling an [Earth](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Earth "Earth") tardigrade that lived in some kind of symbiosis with the spores and was capable of communicating with them, as well as utilizing the mycelial network. These abilities resulted in its function as a sort of "navigator" for the _Glenn_. Emboldened by the breakthrough, Straal reported that he was going to attempt Speirin 900, even though Stamets was concerned about the feasibility and safety of such a massive displacement.

The _Glenn_ managed to travel back and forth into the Beta Quadrant, a ninety light year jump, in 1.3 seconds. However, soon after, the crew of the _Glenn_ hit a Hawking radiation firewall while exiting the mycelial plane, causing the death of its crew.

The _Glenn_ was later scuttled, though Ripper was beamed to _Discovery_ and secured within that ship's own spore drive assembly.

A demonstration of what was possible with the technology at this point in the war included putting someone in a test chamber with spores, and allowing them to see where the spores had been and were going to. The subject quickly cycled through a number of planetary destinations.

After the _Discovery_'s first successful jump using the tardigrade, Stamets transmitted the drive schematics to Starfleet. Production of the drive was begun at a classified Starfleet facility in Jefferson, Iowa on [Earth](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Earth "Earth"). All Federation ships, starbases, and colonie] were placed on alert to search for more tardigrades.

It was possible to use the spore drive even while a ship was traveling at warp speed. The _Discovery_ used this technique to return to the planet Pahvo, going from warp five to a complete stop in the process.

Following the conclusion of the war in 2257, Starfleet decommissioned the drive until a non-Human interface could be developed. In order to investigate one of the red bursts, Captain [Christopher Pike](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Christopher_Pike "Christopher Pike") authorized the use of the drive to travel 51,450 light years to the planet Terralysium, believing the crisis worthy of special dispensation. At the same time, Ensign Sylvia Tilly began working on the possibility of creating a coherent resonator to interact with the spores as a replacement, dark matter-powered navigational interface.

After _Discovery_ was reported destroyed in a battle with an armada of ships controlled by Control, Lieutenant [Spock](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spock "Spock") recommended to Starfleet that all remaining officers with knowledge of these events should be ordered never to speak of _Discovery_ or its spore drive, under penalty of treason.

In the databases of [Starfleet](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Starfleet "Starfleet") in the 32nd century, the _Discovery_ was reported as destroyed as in 2258; however, there was no mention of the spore drive.

In 3189, during the retrofitting of the _Discovery_, a new and improved spore drive was installed. The ship's nacelles would have to be attached before the drive could be activated.

### Current usage[[](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive?veaction=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Current usage")]

Considering the inherent risks of the Spore drive - unintended interdimensional travel, time travel, and the risk to the navigator, the experimental drive has fallen out of favor with Starfleet, and no current vessels in the Federation make use of it. With the continuing advancement of bio-neural technology, this may eventually change, but for the time being, Starfleet's engineering divisions remain focused on the development of [Quantum slipstream drives](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Quantum_slipstream_drive "Quantum slipstream drive") and more conventional warp technology.

### Super-mycelial reactor[[](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive?veaction=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Super-mycelial reactor")]

In the [mirror universe](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Mirror_universe "Mirror universe"), Paul Stamets was able to use the spores to create a reactor. This reactor was then used to power the [Terran Empire](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Terran_Empire "Terran Empire")'s flagship, the [ISS _Charon_](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/ISS_Charon "ISS Charon").

However, Stamets' work misused the mycelial network and gave it a disease that would destroy the network as well as the entire multiverse.

Technical details[[](https://memorydelta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive?veaction=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Technical details")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Spore drive maneuvers were signified by the ship going to black alert.

The reaction cube, in which the spores were injected, was a key part of the drive's operation. One possible density in the chamber was 68%. Another factor in spore drive was spore germination rate.

Excess energy cavitation was part of the initiation process of the spore drive.

A specific spore drive deactivation sequence was needed. Failing to follow the sequence could cause the induction coil to become saturated.

All personnel working around the spore drive were inoculated.

A level 3 diagnostic was run on the entire spore drive every ten hours.

The **Spore Drive**, otherwise known as a **displacement-activated spore hub drive** or **s-drive**, is an advanced form of propulsion technology developed in the mid 23rd century by Starfleet, on the research ships [USS Discovery](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/USS_Discovery "ma:USS Discovery") and [USS Glenn](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/USS_Glenn "ma:USS Glenn"). It is an organic propulsion system utilizing [mycelium spores](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/mycelium_spores "ma:mycelium spores") harvested from _[Prototaxites stellaviatori](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/Prototaxites\_stellaviatori "ma:Prototaxites stellaviatori")_ to jump or leap across the [mycelial network](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/mycelial_network "ma:mycelial network"). During such jumps, a ship is not in normal space but in the [mycelial plane](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/mycelial_plane "ma:mycelial plane"), a discrete layer of subspace.

### Fleet Deployment

*   [USS Discovery](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/USS_Discovery "ma:USS Discovery")
*   [USS Glenn](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/USS_Glenn "ma:USS Glenn")

Basics of Spore Drive
---------------------

[![Image 3: A containment unit, with a blue glow inside it, placed on the dashboard](https://wiki.starbase118.net/wiki/images/thumb/d/d8/Mycelium_Spores.jpg/300px-Mycelium_Spores.jpg)](https://wiki.starbase118.net/wiki/index.php?title=File:Mycelium_Spores.jpg)

_P. stellaviatori_ mycelium spores, key to the drive technology.

### Speed

The experimental Spore Drive has no theoretical speed limit. From an outside perspective, the ship disappears and reappears in another location almost instantly. The USS Glenn completed a jump of 90 light-years in 1.3 seconds, but they hit a [Hawking radiation firewall](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/Hawking_radiation_firewall "ma:Hawking radiation firewall") returning to normal space, which caused the death of the crew.

### Drive stamina

There is no known endurance limitations related to the underlying technology of the Spore Drive. Rather, the stamina is limited to the endurance of the "pilot" navigating the mycelial network. Each jump requires the pilot to "feel" his way through the network. A few jumps in succession isn't difficult. However, when the USS Discovery jumped 133 times in rapid succession, the pilot and chief engineer, [Paul Stamets](http://memory-alpha.org/wiki/Paul_Stamets "ma:Paul Stamets"), suffered extensive physical and mental exhaustion, culminating in a coma.

### Distance

Displacement is measured in Speireins; higher Speireins being associated with large displacement. Jumping is probabilistic, meaning that the longer the jump, the more possible outcomes there are. There is currently no known computer with the processing power capable of making the requisite number of calculations, and so long jumps resulted in navigational instability. Speirein 12 roughly corresponds to a jump in the hundreds of kilometers. Jumps of Speirein 240 and 900 have been attempted, but the results are unknown.

### Current Usage

Considering the inherent risks of the Spore Drive - unintended interdimensional travel, time travel, and the risk to the navigator, the experimental drive has fallen out of favor with Starfleet, and no current vessels in the Federation make use of it. With the continuing advancement of bio-neural technology, this may eventually change, but for the time being, Starfleet's engineering divisions remain focused on the development of [Quantum Slipstream Drives](https://wiki.starbase118.net/wiki/index.php?title=Quantum_Slipstream_Drive "Quantum Slipstream Drive") and more conventional warp technology.

### 23rd century[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmemory-beta.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FUSS_Discovery%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

_Discovery_ was launched from the [San Francisco Fleet Yards](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/San_Francisco_Fleet_Yards "San Francisco Fleet Yards"). [Command](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/CO "CO") was given to [Captain](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Captain "Captain")[Gabriel Lorca](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Gabriel_Lorca_(mirror) "Gabriel Lorca (mirror)") who, unbeknownst to [Starfleet Command](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Starfleet_Command "Starfleet Command"), was in fact a [Terran](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Terran_(mirror) "Terran (mirror)") from the [mirror universe](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Mirror_universe "Mirror universe") and sought to use the ship to return to his universe. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episodes](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Context Is for Kings](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Context_Is_for_Kings "Context Is for Kings")", "[Vaulting Ambition](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Vaulting_Ambition "Vaulting Ambition")")

After [war](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Federation-Klingon_War_of_2256 "Federation-Klingon War of 2256") broke out between the [Federation](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/United_Federation_of_Planets "United Federation of Planets") and the [Klingon Empire](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Klingon_Empire "Klingon Empire") in [May](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/May "May")[2256](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/2256 "2256"), the _Discovery_ and her sister ship, the [USS _Glenn_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Glenn_(NCC-1030) "USS Glenn (NCC-1030)"), were tasked by Starfleet with a top secret mission to develop a new kind of faster-than-light drive utilizing [spores](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore "Spore") from the [fungus](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Fungus "Fungus")[Prototaxites stellaviatori](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Prototaxites_stellaviatori "Prototaxites stellaviatori"). _Discovery_ was assigned to work with [Lieutenant](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Lieutenant "Lieutenant")[Paul Stamets](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Paul_Stamets "Paul Stamets") who managed to have Lorca pull some strings and take on [Cadet](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Cadet "Cadet")[Sylvia Tilly](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Sylvia_Tilly "Sylvia Tilly"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[comic](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Comic "Comic"): "[Discovery Annual 2018](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Discovery_Annual_2018 "Discovery Annual 2018")")

In [November](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/November "November") of the same [year](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Year "Year"), Lorca puppeted events so that the _Discovery_ would cross paths with the [prison](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Prison "Prison")[shuttle](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Shuttle "Shuttle") of former [officer](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Officer "Officer")[Michael Burnham](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Michael_Burnham "Michael Burnham"). Lorca assigned her to work with Stamets' team in developing the new [spore drive](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Spore_drive "Spore drive"), and after joining the [boarding party](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Away_team "Away team") to the disabled USS _Glenn_, Burnham accepted Lorca's offer of parole to work aboard the _Discovery_. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Context Is for Kings](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Context_Is_for_Kings "Context Is for Kings")")

With the help of the captured creature named Ripper and the tech salvaged from the _Glenn_, the _Discovery_ was able to make a significant jump to [Corvan II](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Corvan_II "Corvan II") and saved the [mining](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Mining "Mining")[colony](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Colony "Colony") from a [Klingon](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Klingon "Klingon")attack. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/The_Butcher%27s_Knife_Cares_Not_for_the_Lamb%27s_Cry "The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry")")

When Lorca went off for a meeting at Starfleet Command, his shuttle was ambushed by Klingons and he was taken prisoner. Left in command, [Commander](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Commander "Commander")[Saru](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Saru "Saru") launched a rescue mission where it was revealed that using Ripper to navigate the ship was killing the creature. After Lorca had been retrieved, Ripper was set free with [Ash Tyler](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Ash_Tyler_(Klingon) "Ash Tyler (Klingon)") joining the ship as its new security chief. Stamets meanwhile had injected himself with a sample of Ripper's DNA allowing him to substitute for the creature. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Choose Your Pain](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Choose_Your_Pain "Choose Your Pain")")

In escaping prison, Lorca had made an enemy of [Harry Mudd](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Harry_Mudd "Harry Mudd") who somehow escaped and tracked down Lorca, trapping _Discovery_ in a time loop and intending to sell the ship and its technology off to the Klingons. As a result of Stamets now existing outside the normal time/space continuum, the crew was able to anticipate Mudd's plans and returned him to [Stella](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Stella_Mudd "Stella Mudd") and her, father [Baron](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Baron "Baron")[Grimes](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Grimes_(Baron) "Grimes (Baron)"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Magic to Make the Sanest Man Go Mad](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Magic_to_Make_the_Sanest_Man_Go_Mad "Magic to Make the Sanest Man Go Mad")")

_Discovery_ was later dispatched to [Pahvo](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Pahvo "Pahvo") to try and take advantage of the planet's natural crystalline transmitter in cracking the Klingon [cloaking devices](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Cloaking_device "Cloaking device"). The mission hit a snag when it was discovered that Pahvo was inhabited, with the native [Pahvans](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Pahvan "Pahvan") inviting both Starfleet and the Klingons to their world to try and attain peace. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Si Vis Pacem, Para Bellum](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Si_Vis_Pacem,_Para_Bellum "Si Vis Pacem, Para Bellum")")

Though _Discovery_ was ordered to return to Federation space, Lorca rallied his crew to find a way to break through the cloak so they could defend Pahvo. After an away team had planted sensors aboard the _[Sarcophagus](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Sarcophagus\_(starship) "Sarcophagus (starship)")_, _Discovery_ performed 133 micro-jumps and collected the data needed to penetrate the cloaking device, destroying its foe. Before returning home, Stamets told Lorca he would resign after performing one last spore jump. His hand forced, Lorca overrode the navigational protocols and had _Discovery_ jump to the mirror universe, her arrival sending the [ISS _Discovery_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/ISS_Discovery "ISS Discovery") across to the [prime universe](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Prime_universe "Prime universe"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episodes](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Into the Forest I Go](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Into_the_Forest_I_Go "Into the Forest I Go")", "[Despite Yourself](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Despite_Yourself "Despite Yourself")", "[Vaulting Ambition](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Vaulting_Ambition "Vaulting Ambition")")

After disguising the _Discovery_ as her Terran counterpart, Lorca baited the crew with information on the [USS _Defiant_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Defiant_(NCC-1764) "USS Defiant (NCC-1764)"), having Burnham pose as [her Terran self](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Michael_Burnham_(mirror) "Michael Burnham (mirror)") and take them both to the [ISS _Shenzhou_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/ISS_Shenzhou "ISS Shenzhou"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Despite Yourself](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Despite_Yourself "Despite Yourself")")

[Emperor](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Emperor_of_the_Terran_Empire "Emperor of the Terran Empire")[Philippa Georgiou](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Philippa_Georgiou_(mirror) "Philippa Georgiou (mirror)") eventually discovered Burnham's true identity and offered her all the data on the _Defiant_ in exchange for the blueprints to _Discovery_'s spore drive. Reluctantly, Burnham and Saru agreed to make the trade. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Vaulting Ambition](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Vaulting_Ambition "Vaulting Ambition")")

As _Discovery_ warped to the [ISS _Charon_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/ISS_Charon "ISS Charon"), Burnham contacted them about Lorca's true identity and plan. Saru in turn warned her of the danger the Terran abuse of mycelium was posing. When Burnham managed to lower the _Charon_'s shields, _Discovery_ destroyed her, using the mycelium explosion to jump back to their own universe, albeit nine months after they'd left. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[What's Past Is Prologue](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/What%27s_Past_Is_Prologue "What's Past Is Prologue")")

_Discovery_ arrived back to a grim site, with the Klingons being on the verge of victory. To cripple their foes in one fell swoop, Starfleet Command assigned Emperor Georgiou, having unwillingly been brought aboard _Discovery_ as it jumped between universes, command of _Discovery_ and have her lead a genocidal attack on [Qo'noS](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Qo%27noS "Qo'noS"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[The War Without, The War Within](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/The_War_Without,_The_War_Within "The War Without, The War Within")")

Georgiou's away team soon discovered her orders with Burnham rallying the crew to rebel against orders so blatantly contrary to everything the Federation stood for. Instead, they opted to have [L'Rell](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/L%27Rell "L'Rell") assume control of the Klingon Empire, with her forcing her people to stand down and instead focus on reunifying their race.

Back on [Earth](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Earth "Earth"), the senior staff were each awarded the [Starfleet Medal of Honor](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Starfleet_Medal_of_Honor "Starfleet Medal of Honor") for their heroism. For her first post-war mission, _Discovery_ was assigned to transport [Ambassador](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Ambassador "Ambassador")[Sarek](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Sarek "Sarek") back to [Vulcan](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Vulcan_(planet) "Vulcan (planet)") where she would receive a new captain, only to receive a [priority one](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Priority_one "Priority one") distress call from the [USS _Enterprise_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Enterprise_(NCC-1701) "USS Enterprise (NCC-1701)"), dropping out of warp to meet the other ship. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Will You Take My Hand?](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Will_You_Take_My_Hand%3F "Will You Take My Hand?")")

_Discovery_ was placed under the command of the _Enterprise_'s captain, [Christopher Pike](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Christopher_Pike "Christopher Pike") in order to continue the _Enterprise_'s mission; investigating seven red bursts that had appeared across the galaxy. During the first part of the investigation, _Discovery_ discovered the wreckage of the [USS _Hiawatha_](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/USS_Hiawatha_(NCC-815) "USS Hiawatha (NCC-815)"), rescued Commander [Jett Reno](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Jett_Reno "Jett Reno") and her patients. Following this part of the investigation, _Discovery_ discovered the Earth colony of [New Eden](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/New_Eden "New Eden") on Terralysium in the [Beta Quadrant](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Beta_Quadrant "Beta Quadrant"). (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episodes](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Brother](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Brother "Brother")", "[New Eden](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/New_Eden_(episode) "New Eden (episode)")")

### 32nd century[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmemory-beta.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FUSS_Discovery%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

[![Image 2: Discovery-A in .](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/startrek/images/d/d2/Discovery-A_Shipyards_2294.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20210319214907)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/startrek/images/d/d2/Discovery-A_Shipyards_2294.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210319214907)

_Discovery_-A in [3189](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/3189 "3189").

Upon reestablishing contact with the Federation and Starfleet in the 32nd century _Discovery_ was refitted with 32nd century technology at [Federation Headquarters](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Federation_Headquarters_(station) "Federation Headquarters (station)"). These included integration of programmable matter into controls for improved performance and detached warp nacelles for improved maneuverability. In addition the reaction cube for the spore drive was also upgraded so that it no longer needed to physically attach to the navigator, with nanogel replacing the physical shunts. Following refitting the _Discovery_ was recommissioned with the [registry number](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Registry_number "Registry number") NCC-1031-A. (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Scavengers](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Scavengers_(episode) "Scavengers (episode)")")

Eventually, Commander [Jett Reno](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Jett_Reno "Jett Reno"), one of _Discovery_'s engineers, was able to give the ship's computer a voice. The computer, which had assimilated the data from the Sphere that had required the ship's time travel 930 years into the future, chose to call itself [Zora](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Zora_(artificial_intelligence) "Zora (artificial intelligence)"). (_[ST](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/ST "ST")_[reference](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Reference_work "Reference work"): _[The Star Trek Book](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Star\_Trek\_Book "The Star Trek Book")_)

With the name Zora, which means "dawn" or "new day" in several languages, Zora identified herself as female, developed a fondness for old movies and songs, and also began to experience emotions and empathy for the human crew, whom she viewed as her family. These developments were unprecedented for a ship's computer and made the captain uneasy, though all diagnostic tests run on the computer showed no irregularities. Zora explained that her emotional development was an "organic evolution." She saw herself as distinct from the ship and described herself to Captain [Michael Burnham](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Michael_Burnham "Michael Burnham") as "a sentient organism living inside of a super computer capable of running countless probablistic scenarios." (_[DSC](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/DSC "DSC")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "Stormy Weather")

### Later service[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmemory-beta.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FUSS_Discovery%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

Following the opening of a front in the [Temporal Cold War](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Temporal_Cold_War "Temporal Cold War"), a replica _[Discovery](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Discovery\_(alternates) "Discovery (alternates)")_ was returned to service in [2410](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/2410 "2410"). The ship represented its class during interactions with a ship requisition officer at [Earth Spacedock](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Earth_Spacedock "Earth Spacedock")[shipyards](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Shipyard "Shipyard"). (_[STO](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/STO "STO")_ - _[Victory Is Life](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Victory\_Is\_Life "Victory Is Life")_[mission](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Mission "Mission"): "[Welcome to Earth Spacedock](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Welcome_to_Earth_Spacedock "Welcome to Earth Spacedock")")

At some point, the crew abandoned the ship, and programmed it to stay put. (_[Short Treks](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Short\_Treks "Short Treks")_[episode](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Episode "Episode"): "[Calypso](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Calypso_(episode) "Calypso (episode)")")

During the Temporal Anomaly crisis[Q](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Q "Q") tried to solve, one version of the _Discovery_ appearing at [Saturn](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Saturn "Saturn") circa the year [2380](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/2380 "2380") was Zora's _Discovery_. "Prisoner" Katrina Cornwell ordered [Starfleet](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Starfleet "Starfleet") to investigate. _Discovery_ behaved aggressively until was bested in combat, then opened its shuttlebay. An away team boarded _Discovery_ via shuttle. They found the ship had been deserted. When they tried to commandeer the ship, Zora appeared. A member of the away team charmed Zora, and convinced her to leave Alcor IV and a man named Craft in this timeline alone. (_[ST](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/ST "ST")_[video game](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Video_game "Video game"): _[Timelines](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Timelines "Timelines")_ mission: "Infinity")

Zora welcomed the Alcorian Human Craft onboard when he was stranded in a V'draysh[escape pod](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Escape_pod "Escape pod"). She desired his company but allowed him to leave with a [Class C shuttlecraft](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Class_C_shuttlecraft "Class C shuttlecraft"), which she dubbed _[Funny Face](https://memory-beta.fandom.com/wiki/Funny\_Face\_(shuttle) "Funny Face (shuttle)")_. Spore drive
-----------

[![Image 3: The performing a spore jump](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sto_gamepedia/images/e/e1/Secrets_-_U.S.S._Glenn_arrival.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20181202223608)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sto_gamepedia/images/e/e1/Secrets_-_U.S.S._Glenn_arrival.png/revision/latest?cb=20181202223608)

The [U.S.S. _Glenn_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/U.S.S._Glenn "U.S.S. Glenn") performing a spore jump

The **Spore drive** is the common term for a **displacement-activated spore hub drive**, an organic propulsion system which utilizes the mycelium spores of [Prototaxites stellaviatori](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Prototaxites_stellaviatori "Prototaxites stellaviatori"). It allowed a vessel to instantaneously jump to any point in the universe. Both the [Federation](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Federation "Federation") and the [Klingons](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Klingon "Klingon") covertly used this technology during [Burnham's War](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Federation-Klingon_War_(2256-57) "Federation-Klingon War (2256-57)") to gain an advantage over the other side. The technology was no longer in use by the [2260s](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/23rd_century "23rd century").

In the [25th century](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/25th_century "25th century"), the [Elachi](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Elachi "Elachi") make limited, but technically advanced use of spore drives on some of their ships due to their origin in the [Mycelial network](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mycelial_network "Mycelial network").

Background[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsto.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FSpore_drive%3Faction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The technology was developed by [Justin Straal](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Justin_Straal "Justin Straal") and [Paul Stamets](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Paul_Stamets "Paul Stamets"), jointly deployed on the [U.S.S. _Glenn_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/U.S.S._Glenn "U.S.S. Glenn") and [U.S.S. _Discovery_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/U.S.S._Discovery "U.S.S. Discovery"). The _Glenn_ managed to perfect the drive through the acquisition of a creature referred to as a [tardigrade](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Tardigrade "Tardigrade"). However the _Glenn'_ s crew, along with Straal, were all killed in an accident that ensued during a failed jump. (_["Context is for Kings"](https://memory-alpha.fandom.com/wiki/Context\_is\_for\_Kings "w:c:memory-alpha:Context is for Kings")_)

Prior to their demise, [J'Ula](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/J%27Ula "J'Ula") of [House Mo'Kai](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/House_Mo%27Kai "House Mo'Kai") succeeded in stealing this technology from the _Glenn_. She modified it to function as a weapon and placed it on the [I.K.S. _Lukara_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/I.K.S._Lukara "I.K.S. Lukara"). _( [“Secrets”](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:\_Secrets "Mission: Secrets"))_ Her attempt at using it during the [attack on Starbase One](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:_Defense_of_Starbase_One "Mission: Defense of Starbase One") failed, due to Straal having corrupted the data she stole, resulting in her time displacement to the [25th century](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/25th_century "25th century") along with another [Starfleet](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/DSC_Starfleet "DSC Starfleet") vessel (The player's DSC Starfleet vessel). _( [“Downfall”](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:\_Downfall "Mission: Downfall"))_

The _Discovery_ acquired the tardigrade from the _Glenn_ after the disaster and its crew managed to successfully use the technology in the following months. However, after the tardigrade started dying, they were forced to find an alternative to its role as a navigator throughout the mycelial plane. Stamets conducted an [illegal genetic augmentation](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Augment "Augment") on himself and took over that role personally. (_["Choose Your Pain"](https://memory-alpha.fandom.com/wiki/Choose\_Your\_Pain "w:c:memory-alpha:Choose Your Pain")_)

The technology was used intermittently after that, but was eventually classified with the disappearance of the Discovery. (_["Such Sweet Sorrow"](https://memory-alpha.fandom.com/wiki/Such\_Sweet\_Sorrow,\_Part\_2\_(episode) "w:c:memory-alpha:Such Sweet Sorrow, Part 2 (episode)")_) The technology was only uncovered once more with the appearance of [J'Ula](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/J%27Ula "J'Ula") in the 25th century and her pollution of the [Mycelial network](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mycelial_network "Mycelial network"). After this, it was identified that some Elachi, apparently from the network, had a greater mastery of the technology than the Federation had developed.

### Jump to the Mirror universe[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsto.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FSpore_drive%3Faction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

The Discovery's jumps included one to the [mirror universe](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mirror_universe "Mirror universe"). There, the [Terran Empire](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Terran_Empire "Terran Empire") of the [23rd century](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/23rd_century "23rd century") had been pursuing similar research, but instead sought to use the mycelial plane as a power source. The Discovery's jump caused the [I.S.S. _Discovery_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/I.S.S._Discovery "I.S.S. Discovery") to jump to [25th century](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/25th_century "25th century") prime universe. (_[“Para Pacem”](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:\_Para\_Pacem "Mission: Para Pacem")_)

When the [I.S.S. _Charon_](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/I.S.S._Charon "I.S.S. Charon"), which used a mycelial reactor, was destroyed in mirror universe, its wreckage was thrown forward to [2410](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/2410 "2410") where [Captain Killy](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Sylvia_Tilly_(mirror) "Sylvia Tilly (mirror)") was attempting to bring reinforcements to. However many Terrans who made that journey ended up cocooned in mycelian strands. _( [“Illusion of Communication”](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:\_Illusion\_of\_Communication "Mission: Illusion of Communication"), [“Pahvo Dissension”](https://sto.fandom.com/wiki/Mission:\_Pahvo\_Dissension "Mission: Pahvo Dissension"))_

10 most disliked moments in Star Trek: Discovery, ranked

Let's look at ten specific moments and decisions from Discovery that left a bit of a bitter aftertaste for some viewers.

2. Introduction of the Spore Drive
----------------------------------

Let's talk about something that made a lot of fans raise an eyebrow: the Spore Drive.

Picture this: you're chilling in your captain's chair, sipping on some Romulan ale, when suddenly, the crew whips out this wild new technology called the Spore Drive. Now, you might be thinking, "Cool! More futuristic tech, right?" Well, not exactly.

See, the Spore Drive is like something straight out of science fiction. It taps into this funky network of spores that exist across the universe, allowing ships to jump to different places almost instantly. Sounds too good to be true? Well, that's because it kinda is. Now, don't get me wrong, Star Trek has always been about pushing the boundaries of what's possible. But with the Spore Drive, they took a bit of a leap (pun intended). Some long-time fans started scratching their heads, thinking, "Hold up, how does this fit into the whole Star Trek universe?"

You see, one of the things that makes Star Trek so beloved is its rich history and continuity. Each new series or movie builds on what came before, creating this intricate web of lore that fans adore. But the Spore Drive? It felt like it was breaking some of those rules. For starters, it's never been mentioned before in any other Star Trek show or movie. And we're talking about a technology that can essentially teleport ships across the galaxy. You'd think someone would have brought it up at some point, right?

Plus, the whole idea of using spores to zip around space like a cosmic Uber just seemed a bit... out there. I mean, we're mostly used to warp drive, not instantaneous teleporting. So, yeah, the introduction of the Spore Drive sparked a bit of a debate among fans. Some thought it was a bold new direction for the series, while others felt like it was straying too far from what makes Star Trek, well, Star Trek. Myself, I thought it was pretty neat, but I also have a hard time accepting that this life-changing technology was never brought up again in "future" Trek (don't forget, _Discovery_ takes place **before**_The Original Series_).

But hey, whether you love it or hate it, you gotta admit, the Spore Drive definitely got people talking. And isn't that what Star Trek is all about? Boldly going where no one has gone before, even if it means jumping through a few spores along the way.

The Science of Star Trek: Discovery’s Mycelial Network
======================================================

Posted in [Pop Culture](https://twincitiesgeek.com/category/news/pop-culture/), [Science & Tech](https://twincitiesgeek.com/category/news/sci-tech/) By [Joe Praska](https://twincitiesgeek.com/author/jpraska/ "Posts by Joe Praska") On April 11, 2018

Warp drives, subspace networks, inertial dampeners, transporters, holodecks, universal translators, transparent aluminum. With _Star Trek_, the list of high-tech concepts and gadgets (both the more well-thought-out and grounded ideas and the [slightly less realistic](http://www.slate.com/blogs/bad_astronomy/2013/05/16/star_trek_science_mistakes.html)) is nearly endless. Now, thanks to the most recent iteration of the franchise, _Star Trek: Discovery_, words such as “spore drive” and “mycelial network” can be added to the list.

[![Image 2: Star Trek: Discovery season 1 poster by James Dimmock](https://i0.wp.com/twincitiesgeek.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/Star-Trek-Discovery-CBS-All-Access-400x600.jpg?resize=341%2C512)](https://i0.wp.com/twincitiesgeek.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/Star-Trek-Discovery-CBS-All-Access.jpg)_Star Trek: Discovery_ on CBS All Access. _Photo by James Dimmock. © 2017 CBS Interactive._

Despite taking us to the past in terms of _Trek_ canon, _Star Trek: Discovery_ pushed us to look forward in how we think about the plausibility of space travel and how we view the space in which our planet exists. With the USS _Discovery’_s experimental [displacement-activated spore hub drive](http://memory-alpha.wikia.com/wiki/Spore_drive) (mostly just referred to as the spore drive) and the exploration of what came to be known as the mycelial network, the writers attempted to assert that—at least in the _Star Trek_ universe—wormholes and warp drives weren’t the only ways to get from point A to point B.

As Captain Lorca (Jason Isaacs) describes in the third episode of the series, “Context is for Kings,” the mycelial network can be imagined as a “microscopic web that spans the entire cosmos. An intergalactic ecosystem. An infinite number of roads leading everywhere.” With that, _Discovery_’s spore drive then served as a kind of organic propulsion system by which the ship could attempt to navigate these “infinite roads,” allowing for near instantaneous travel. In the series, the ideas behind the spore drive came from the research of Dr. Paul Stamets (Anthony Rapp), who, along with his research partner, chose to think of physics and biology as interchangeable at the quantum level. Through this thinking, and generating equations based in quantum astrophysics and biochemistry, the two were able to theorize that, as _Star Trek_ wiki [Memory Alpha](http://memory-alpha.wikia.com/wiki/Spore_drive) says, “spores were not only the progenitors of [panspermia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panspermia), but also the building blocks of energy across the universe,” and thus something starships could theoretically use to travel.

As the first season of _Star Trek: Discovery_ progressed, viewers learned more and more about the spore drive and the ecology of the mycelial network, as well as the difficulties of using it as a tool for navigation. While the concept as a narrative element within the story was fascinating, the question becomes: does real-life science back it up?

On an episode of [_After Trek_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Trek), _Star Trek: Discovery_ producer Aaron Herberts said, “Everything we do on _Star Trek_ comes out of character, and also as much as we can ground in science, so, shameless plug: get Paul Stamets’s book [_Mycelium Running_](https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/mycelium-running-paul-stamets/1101758001?ean=9781580085793#/).” Not dissimilar from Rapp’s Paul Stamets in the series, the real-life Paul Stamets, author of the aforementioned _Mycelium Running,_ is a pioneering researcher in the field of mycology and a vocal advocate for the applications of mushroom and fungi research.

In his book, Stamets introduces us to mycelium, which he describes as the “neurological network of nature.” Mycelium is a thin web of cells made up of numerous [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypha) (or “branching filamentous structures”), that, at one point in its life cycle, produces mushrooms.

[![Image 4: A microscopic view of strands of mycelia.](https://i0.wp.com/twincitiesgeek.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/16347-microscopic-photo-of-fungus-pv-600x401.jpg?resize=449%2C300)](https://i0.wp.com/twincitiesgeek.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/16347-microscopic-photo-of-fungus-pv.jpg)Photomicrograph depicting the microscopic mycelia of a fungus. [_freestockphotos.biz_](http://www.freestockphotos.biz/stockphoto/16347)

Throughout _Mycelium Running_, Stamets posits that this mycelial network is much more than a collection of cells that ultimately grow mushrooms and other kinds of fungi. The hyphae that make up mycelium are continuously interweaving and branching out from each other, which “infuse habitats with information-sharing membranes.” Frequently referencing mycelia as “nature’s Internet,” Stamets believes that “mycelium operates at a level of complexity that exceeds the computational powers of our most advanced supercomputers.” He asserts that, because of this natural intelligence contained within the network, mycelial webs have the potential to act as a consciousness with which to develop a kind of cross-species communication, and could be used as “information platforms for mycoengineered ecosystems.”

On top of potentially existing as a complex communication interface, Stamets cultivated mycelium as tool for creating fuel—or “econol,” as he refers to it—as well. In his 2008 [TED Talk](https://www.ted.com/talks/paul_stamets_on_6_ways_mushrooms_can_save_the_world/transcript?language=en#t-168586), he describes a mycelial process he discovered in which he was able to convert cellulose into fungal sugars, effectively “generating ethanol from cellulose using mycelium as an intermediary.” So while none of this quite matches up to _Discovery’_s use of its mycelial network as a means of near-instantaneous transportation, one can extrapolate where the idea came from when looking at real-life Stamets’s theories on mycelium as “nature’s Internet,” and its use in creating a means for propulsion in econol.

With the foundational research for the mycelial network itself based in real-life Stamets’s ideas, _Star Trek: Discovery_ spent several of its earlier episodes on finding out a way to effectively navigate its expansive hyphae that stretch endlessly throughout the cosmos. The series first gives us a navigator in the form of the large tardigrade-like creature discovered in episode 3. The tardigrade was able to successfully traverse the network, as it shared elements of its DNA with the fungal elements of mycelium. This concept checks out, according to a 2015 study [published in _PNAS_](http://www.pnas.org/content/early/2015/11/18/1510461112), stating that a large percentage of the tardigrade genome is made up of “diverse bacteria as well as plants, fungi, and Archaea.” Furthermore, as the series progressed, we learn through _Trek-_Stamets that a human linked up with the ship’s spore drive can also successfully navigate the network. This also makes sense, as its been [shown](https://www.scienceabc.com/nature/how-are-mushrooms-more-similar-to-humans-than-plants.html) that humans and fungi share a common ancestor—one that puts us closer in relation to fungi, geneologicaly, than fungi are to plants.

Many ideas in the various _Star Trek_ iterations are often outlandish and even a little silly, but there has always been a concerted effort to ground at least some of it in reality. As it stands, _Star Trek: Discovery_ is no exception and continues to build on not only real life scientific concepts, but ideas that are newer to the franchise as a whole. With the foundational work that season 1 has laid out so far for the series, it’s exciting to think about where _Discovery’_s writers will take us as the journey continues.
